llm.summary: The skill mostly does what its README/description promise (a local stock UI and analyzers), but there are mismatches between the declared requirements and the actual code and runtime behavior — notably undeclared AI API usage that will transmit local portfolio context to external providers — so review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (stock quotes, limit-up tracking, portfolio management, UI) match the code: FastAPI backend, Vue frontend, local JSON store, pywencai/py requests for market data. The included sync and analytics modules are consistent with a stock assistant. Minor note: the skill supports multiple remote AI providers (OpenAI, SiliconFlow, Zhipu, Minimax) which is coherent with the 'AI Assistant' capability, but the registry metadata declared no required env vars/credentials while the code clearly expects AI_PROVIDER/AI_API_KEY/etc. — this is an inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions (SKILL.md + start scripts) direct the service to load local portfolio_data.json and include portfolio/watchlist items into the AI chat context, then call remote AI provider endpoints when AI is enabled. That means private/local portfolio data would be sent to third‑party APIs if a user sets AI_API_KEY and AI_PROVIDER. The start/install scripts also suggest globally installing jsdom (npm -g) which modifies the host environment. Other actions (sync script) perform extensive network scraping (iterating many codes) which is expected for data sync but can be noisy.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no registry 'install' spec, but the bundle includes scripts/install.sh and start scripts that run pip/npm and may install jsdom globally. The sources are included in the package (no unknown remote download URLs shown). Installing global npm packages is a host-level change — expected for pywencai but worth reviewing the install script before running.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars, yet code and SKILL.md reference several environment variables (AI_PROVIDER, AI_API_KEY, AI_MODEL, AI_BASE_URL, NODE_PATH). If AI_PROVIDER is set to anything other than 'silence', the AI_API_KEY is required and the service will send user portfolio/watchlist context to the configured external API. That is a significant privacy/credential scope mismatch and should be considered before enabling remote AI providers.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request system-wide privilege changes. It writes to its own local JSON files (portfolio_data.json, stock_codes.json) — expected for the app. It does suggest installing global npm packages (jsdom) which affects the system but is not an elevated privilege flag within the registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package is a plausible local stock assistant, but pay attention to three things before installing or running it:

1) Environment mismatch: The registry says no credentials are required, but the code and docs expect AI_PROVIDER and AI_API_KEY (and optionally AI_BASE_URL/AI_MODEL). If you configure an external AI provider and set AI_API_KEY, your portfolio and watchlist (the local portfolio_data.json contents) will be sent to that provider as part of the chat context. If you want to avoid sending private data, set AI_PROVIDER=silence or do not provide an API key.

2) Review install scripts: scripts/install.sh and backend/start.sh may install dependencies (including npm -g jsdom). Installing global npm packages affects your system; inspect those scripts and run them in a controlled/sandboxed environment (container, VM) if possible.

3) Network & privacy: sync_all_stocks.py will perform broad network calls (scanning many stock codes) and the backend fetches remote market APIs; expect network activity. If you have sensitive local files, note that the app reads/writes portfolio_data.json and stock_codes.json. Back up any data and inspect the files before and after running.

If you want to proceed: (a) inspect scripts/install.sh and start.sh contents, (b) run in an isolated environment, (c) prefer AI_PROVIDER=silence for local-only behavior, and (d) only supply API keys to trustworthy providers and understand that the skill will include portfolio context in requests.
